newsitem.title: USA: Few foreign crudes still seeking US buyers in July.
newsitem.headline: Few foreign crudes still seeking US buyers in July.

text.p: A few cargoes of foreign crude arriving in July were still looking for U.S. buyers on Thursday, although many refiners had already wrapped up their requirements for the month, traders said.
"If refiners aren't already wrapped up, they should be soon," a Gulf Coast trader said.
A trading house was offering a Nigerian Forcados cargo of around 900,000 barrels for July 10-20 delivery, traders said.
Forcados was last pegged around 20 cents over dated Brent on an fob basis.
A Norwegian company was also offering North Sea Oseberg for mid-month delivery, traders said.
Overall, North Sea and West African offerings remained scant, reflecting the tight trans-Atlantic arbitrage. Many Nigerian cargoes were also snapped up by Asian refiners in recent weeks.
The August spread between West Texas Intermediate and Brent was around $1.10-20 a barrel on Thursday afternoon, down five to 10 cents from late on Wednesday.
Dated Brent, meanwhile, was assessed around 30 cents under August Brent, up from around minus 55 cents earlier this week, narrowing trans-Atlantic opportunities even further.
The tight arb continued to turn market attention to Latin America.

Occidental resumed normal operations at the Cano Limon oil field in Colombia following back-to-back rebel bombings of the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline, although liftings are expected to be delayed by one to two days.
Two crude tankers that had been unable to load at Covenas have also resumed normal operations, trade sources said.
The two Panamax tankers are the Santa Panaglia, which is bound for Peru on behalf of Spain's Repsol and the Harrier, which is bound for the U.S. for Shell.
As a result of the shut-in, however, Ecopetrol was expected late on Thursday to issue a new lifting schedule, reflecting delays of one to two days.
Occidental, which operates the 215,000 barrels per day (bpd) field, was forced to temporarily shut in output after Tuesday's blast, the second in a week.

Meanwhile, a U.S. company bought a cargo of Cano Limon crude from a European company at around $2.55 under WTI/Cushing. The cargo is scheduled to load July 22-24, but is likely to get pushed back by a day or two as a result of the pipeline bombings, traders said.
Finally, Ecopetrol sold a Vasconia cargo loading July 26-30 at around September WTI minus $3.40 a barrel fob, traders said.
